newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - January 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - January 22.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Taiwan provincial governor James Soong, who tendered resignation at end 1997, returns to work but says he has not changed his mind to resign.
Shipping links between Taiwan and Hong Kong will carry over July 1997.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - James Soong returns to work but says he is waiting for the central government's approval on resignation.
Former Chiayi police chief is sentenced to six and a half years in prison over video game scandal.
LIBERTY TIMES - Central government urges parliament to revise law to drop provincial governor re-election.
Finance ministry and justice ministry will intensify examinations on money remittance to avoid money laundering.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Import tax shows 6.8 percent negative growth in second half of 1996/97 (July/June) fiscal year.
Shipping officials and businessmen start conference today (Wednesday) in Hong Kong to discuss technical issues on Taiwan-China shipping links.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Postal fund bureau will start loan business in March.
Assets in over-the-counter market hit over one trillion.
